Q: Why I am getting different date when I am changing my column with whole number data type into date data type? A:

Do not directly change from whole number to date, powerbi will interpret it as days since 1899. Instead create a custom column and use this formula #date([column name)], 1, 1), it will create a new column with correct year

Q: How to install deb822 apt repositories using ansible's apt_repository module? A:

A brief summary, based on @JohnRDOrazio's answer using qbittorrent-stable repository

- name: Get repository key fingerprint
  ansible.builtin.uri:
    url: https://api.launchpad.net/devel/~qbittorrent-team/+archive/ubuntu/qbittorrent-stable
    return_content: true
    method: GET
    headers:
      Accept: 'application/json'
  register: repository_key_fingerprint

- name: Add repository
  become: true
  ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
    state: present
    name: "qbittorrent-stable-{{ ansible_facts['distribution_release'] }}"
    types: deb
    uris: https://ppa.launchpadcontent.net/qbittorrent-team/qbittorrent-stable/ubuntu
    suites: "{{ ansible_facts['distribution_release'] }}"
    components: main
    signed_by: |
      {{ lookup('ansible.builtin.url',
      'https://keyserver.ubuntu.com/pks/lookup?op=get&search=0x' + repository_key_fingerprint.json.signing_key_fingerprint,
      split_lines=False) }}

Q: Button with GlassProminentButtonStyle without the text effect A:

This behaviour of automatically glassifying the button label is only limited to very specific views like text and images. Most other kinds of views won't be glassified.

Simply setting the foreground style to .foreground removes the glass effect on the label,

HStack {
    Image(systemName: "trash")
    Text("Delete")
}
.foregroundStyle(.foreground)

Using .drawingGroup() also works.

Q: Pandas dataframe conditional value assignemnt leads to error when there are exactly 2 rows in the dataframe A:

Ok if I define the column types, then it solves the issue:

df['interpretation'] = pd.Series(dtype='string')
df['class'] = pd.Series(dtype='string')

It's is still puzzling that it only fails for 2 rows. With 1 or 3 or more rows meeting the same condition (>0.4), the column types would in theory still be undefined as well and lead to the error but it doesn't. Only with exactly 2 rows. So it does seem like a pandas edge-case bug.

Q: How to add a title to a faceted bar chart with Seaborn's object interface A:

It looks like seaborn community is pretty much inactive. I figured out that I can add a title via matplotlib, though:

f = plt.figure()
so.Plot(df, x="A").facet("B").add(so.Bar(), so.Count()).on(f).plot()
f.suptitle("Super awesome plot")
plt.show()

Q: How to resolve an App Store Connect that I'm missing required icon files. Validation failed error A:

Most reliable fix for this problem is:

  1. Delete:

    Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset

  2. In Xcode:
    File → New → App Icon

  3. Re-add:

    • 1024x1024 first

    • Then drag a 1024 master image into entire set (Xcode auto generates sizes)

  4. Re-select:
    Target → General → App Icons Source → AppIcon

  5. Clean build:

    Shift + Cmd + K

  6. Delete Derived Data:

    ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData

  7. Archive again

    If Still Failing

    Inspect the built archive directly:

    1. Archive

    2. Right-click archive

    3. Show in Finder

    4. Right-click → Show Package Contents

    5. Go to:

      Products/Applications/YourApp.app

    Check if files exist:

    AppIcon60x60@2x.png  (120x120)
AppIcon76x76@2x.png  (152x152)
1024 icon is not included here normally (App Store only)

    If missing → asset not compiled.

Q: Objects.equals(null, null); should return false A:

Ah this is maybe similar to the expression 0^0 (zero to the power of zero). The result could be 0, because zero multiplied with anything is 0. But it could be 1 too, because anything to the power of 0 is 1. So the best answer could be a set of two values: 0^0 = {0, 1}. But if you were forced to give one value 1 would be a better answer than 0, because limit of x^x where x goes against infinity is 1. In a smililar way the best answer for Objects.equals(null, null) would be a tripple: {false, true, unknown}. But I think for the most practical cases false would be the better answer.
